# Kukkuṭajātaka (Ja 448)
**ID:** Ja 448
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)
**Collection:** Suttas-Late-1
**Title (Pali):** Kukkuṭajātaka
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/ja448
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul9.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Kukkuṭajātaka* (Ja 448), titled in English *The Chicken*, is a narrative from the Pali Jātaka collection [SuttaCentral]. Set at the Bamboo Grove (Veḷuvana) in Rājagaha, the frame story relates that the monks in the Hall of Truth were discussing Devadatta's wicked schemes, specifically his deployment of archers in an attempt to assassinate the Buddha [Fausböll 1887; SuttaCentral]. The Buddha intervened to declare that Devadatta had also sought to kill him in a previous life, introducing the story of the past with the opening verse *Nāsmase katapāpamhi* ("Trust not in those [who have done evil]") [Fausböll 1887; SuttaCentral]. In that past life, the Bodhisatta was reborn as a wild fowl or cock (*kukkuṭa*) and Devadatta as a predatory hawk (*senaka*); after the hawk attempted to entrap and destroy the cock, the cock outwitted his predator and compelled him to flee [Fausböll 1887]. The Jātaka is also attested in the mural sequence of the Pagan period in Burma, where it appears in its traditional canonical sequence following the *Mahādhammapālajātaka* (Ja 447) [Win Than Tun 2002].
In terms of parallels and text reuse, SuttaCentral identifies Ja 383 (also titled *Kukkuṭajātaka*) as a direct passage-level parallel, and notes narrative resemblances with the *Vānarajātaka* (Ja 342) and *Sulasājātaka* (Ja 419) [SuttaCentral]. Machine-assisted analysis via DharmaNexus indicates that the verses of Ja 448 are reused extensively in the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* and in the later Pali didactic compilation *Nāradakkhadīpanī* (*Nīti-gantha-saṅgaho*) [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, DharmaNexus aligns individual gnomic segments of the text with Tibetan gnomic works preserved in the Tanjur, including the *Nītiśāstra* (D4335) and *Cāṇakyarājanītiśāstra* (D4334), as well as an alignment with the Chinese *Shanshengzi jing* (T 17) [DharmaNexus].

- Passage-level parallels (SuttaCentral): Ja 383 Kukkuṭajātaka
- Resembling parallels (SuttaCentral): Ja 342 Vānarajātaka; Ja 419 Sulasājātaka
- Text reuse within the Pali corpus (DharmaNexus): Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā (Catuttho bhāgo) (Atk S0513a4) (§1.1–7.4 ↔ §482–501); Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā (Tatiyo bhāgo) (Atk S0513a3) (§9.1–10.4 ↔ §2389–2393); Nīti-gantha-saṅgaho Naradakkhadīpanī (Anya E1009n) (§9.1–9.4 ↔ §371–374)
